## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized mason wasp characterized by its black body with reddish markings, narrow waist, folded wings, and compact solitary-wasp appearance. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, yards, and other open or semi-open habitats with flowers, shrubs, and available nesting cavities. Females nest in preexisting holes, hollow stems, or small cavities, stocking the nest cells with paralyzed caterpillars or other soft-bodied larvae for their young, while adults visit flowers for nectar and help regulate herbivorous insects.
